question: Which attributed semantic blockers are causally sufficient to open the real branch-8 zero-new-via local repair, and does a failed ablation expose blockers hidden behind the original frontier?

implementation.search_rule: breadth-first: suppress one ranked semantic owner from the current failed frontier, rerun the exact bounded local search, and let each new failure expose children not visible at its parent frontier

semantic_actions.footprint_pad: remove all pad obstacles owned by the footprint; this is a conservative component-motion counterfactual because connected foreign copper remains
semantic_actions.foreign_net_copper: remove that foreign net's track/via obstacles while retaining its pads; this models a bounded rip-up counterfactual

implementation.transaction_rule: all ablations are counterfactual_only=true and selectable=false; no suppressed object is removed from a native board candidate

reduced_controls.single_wall: one movable full-height pad wall is a sufficient size-1 cut
reduced_controls.hidden_second_wall: the original frontier contains only WALL_A; after suppressing it, the failed child exposes WALL_B, and WALL_A+WALL_B is the first sufficient size-2 cut

front.interpretation: none of the conflict-guided one- or two-owner cuts generated within the per-failure rank bound opens F.Cu; component-only C4/R19 ablations and every tested pair also fail

back.interpretation: GND alone opens B.Cu; the four found GND pairs are redundant supersets and do not constitute additional minimum cuts

worked: the hidden-wall regression proves that child failures can discover blockers absent from the original frontier
the real B.Cu result converts GND from a high-hit correlation into a causal sufficient counterfactual
the real F.Cu result exhausts every generated size-1/2 trial under the declared rank bound instead of stopping at an arbitrary trial limit
every original failure and every counterfactual trial has a paired front/back SVG and PNG; found paths are green and suppressed obstacles disappear from the rendered model
limits: suppressing an object is not an implementable move: component poses, attached copper, foreign-net connectivity, and native DRC are deliberately not changed in these trials
the front conclusion is bounded to the 50 conflict-guided sets generated with nine ranked blockers per failure and cut size at most two; it is not a global minimum-cut proof
counterfactual work is expensive: 1,063,848 front and 413,194 back expansions versus 19,126 and 10,788 for the original failures
GND is still represented as routed tree copper; a future filled-zone/plane policy can change both the obstacle topology and the appropriate repair action
the 44.152543 mm B.Cu path is only proof of reachability after GND suppression, not a quality-selected or native-complete board
critical_evaluation.next: use the B.Cu GND result as a small plane-aware/rip-up-and-restore experiment, and generate a true mixed front action that combines foreign-net rerouting with declared component motion before retrying the target repair; do not merely increase cut size without an action model
